column1: # --- malformed manifest entries: refusing them is the CORRECT answer ---
# Both lack a usable placeholder, so they designate a path anchored outside every root we know.
# SKIP rather than MISS because the fixture builder will not create them either — there is nowhere
# inside the scratch tree they could go. Returning nothing makes the user pick a folder; returning
# "/AppData/..." or "E:\AppData\..." would look authoritative and be wrong.
Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator
Ironclads: American Civil War
# --- name matching: a shortcut carries whatever the user typed (4th column = the spelling asked for)
# DQ3 is THE case: added to Steam as a non-Steam game, spelled without the manifest's hyphen.
Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake
Celeste
column3: pure case difference must still match

column1: # --- Saves loose in the install directory: the answer is the whole game, so it must not win ---
# Found on a Deck (2026-08-09): Cave Story+ was mapped to its install folder. Resolving <base>
# itself would sync the game, and restore's delete pass would then prune another machine's
# installation to match it.
# Cave Story+ is the DQ3 shape all over again — a bad candidate outranking a good one. It has four
# save paths: three loose files under <base>, and a real Documents folder. Dropping the install
# directory is what lets the Documents folder win, so this is a HIT that used to be WRONG.
Cave Story+
column3: <base> loose files must not beat the real Documents folder
